messages:
marta: quick question — when we surface per-route quota controls in the console, should tenant admins also be able to attach routing fallbacks (eg. model variant fallback, region fallback) at the same granular level?
ben: my 2¢: i think routing fallbacks are operational and risky to expose widely. maybe an opt-in advanced toggle for tenant-admins? :thinking_face:
sara: agree with @ben. also telemetry-wise we need to tag requests with the policy id if we let tenants configure it, otherwise regression debugging is impossible.
kevin: +1 on tagging. if tenant-configured policy exists we should add header x-rw-policy-id and add to trace logs. platform-only policies can have system namespace.
yash: from API perspective the permissions model already has scope strings like "routes:write" and "policies:manage:platform". we could add "policies:manage:tenant" and gate that in the backend. simple boolean check in policy service.
marta: that makes sense. UX question: do we put fallback controls inline in the route editor or behind a dedicated "advanced routing" modal? inline might be noisy for 90% of users.
ben: modal + a small inline summary badge ("fallbacks configured") seems nice. clicking opens modal with canary + fallbacks + cost estimate.
sara: cost estimate is key. if tenant config chooses larger model for fallback we need to show incremental cost per 1k tokens. Otherwise support tickets blow up.
kevin: can we reuse Optimize's pricing calc endpoint? example payload: ```POST /optimize/estimate {"model":"gptx-16", "fallback":"gptx-32", "avg_tokens":1200}``` response returns per-token delta.
yash: yep reuse is fine, just need to ensure permissions for calling the endpoint when previewing in the console — don't leak pricing detail to viewers without billing scope.
console-bot: note: design review scheduled Thu 11am in #eng-platform-design.
marta: one more API debate: should the route object carry the policy itself (embedded) or a policy_ref id?
ben: policy_ref id is cleaner for rollback/rollouts and reusing the same policy across routes. embedding is simpler for one-offs though.
sara: rollout UX wants referential policies so we can show diffs, do A/B, and run telemetry cohorts. referential wins for telemetry.
kevin: agreed. implementation detail: policy entity needs versioning (v1, v2) and immutable snapshots so old route configs reference the snapshot id.
yash: i'll sketch the API: ```POST /policies {"name":"tenant-fallbacks","rules":[...], "tenant_id":"t-123"} -> {"policy_id":"p-789","snapshot_id":"s-001"}``` then route object stores snapshot_id.
marta: lovely. last concern — permissions: who can attach a policy to a route? tenant owners? specific role?
ben: add a permission check: "routes:attach_policy" scoped to role and route namespace. UI should hide controls unless user has that permission.
sara: and telemetry: emit event policy.attached (user, route, policy_snapshot, method) for audit and cost monitoring.
kevin: +1, also emit policy.applied_at runtime tag on requests so we can attribute latency/cost to policies in dashboards.
marta: ok action items: @yash draft API payload + permission matrix, @kevin add trace header and runtime tagging, @sara add telemetry/events spec, @ben prototype modal summary copy. I'll file a tiny RFC by EOD. :thumbsup:
